transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you for seeing me. Um... I hope I'm in the right place for this. I don't want to waste your time if it's not a big deal, but... I guess I came in because I've just been being a little hard on myself lately. 

I work as a systems analyst, and I just keep beating myself up, thinking that... well, that I'm not really senior material. It sounds a bit silly to say out loud, but I feel like I've just fooled everyone into thinking I could handle more than I actually can. 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
How long have you been feeling this way about yourself? Have these thoughts been constant or do they come and go?

Um... well, if I really look back at it... I guess these sort of low, guilty periods have been hanging around for a while. Not constantly, though! They definitely come and go. I really don't want to make it sound worse than it is, I mean, I'm still managing things okay at work for the most part. 

But... maybe for about eleven months now, off and on? I'm sorry if I should have come in sooner for this, I just kept thinking I could shake it off on my own and didn't want to bother anyone with it. Is that the kind of timeline you were looking for? I hope I'm answering your questions right.
Can you describe what goes through your mind during these low periods? Specifically, do you find yourself feeling worthless or guilty, even when things seem to be going okay on the surface?

Um, yeah, that's... that's exactly it, actually. Like I was saying when I first sat down—and I hope it's okay if I sort of repeat myself here, I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right—it's mostly just me beating myself up. 

Even when a project goes fine on the surface, my mind just goes straight to... well, to thinking that I'm not really senior material. I get this awful, guilty feeling that I've just fooled everyone at the company into thinking I could handle way more than I actually can. I really try to just keep my head down and push through it so I don't bother my team or make a big deal out of nothing, but... yeah, that's what goes through my head. 

I know it probably sounds a bit foolish when I say it like that. Is that the kind of detail you needed? I can try to explain it better if that wasn't clear enough.
During these low periods, do you find yourself losing interest or pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?

Um... yeah, I guess maybe a little bit? I hope I'm not making too big a deal out of it, but... well, usually, I really look forward to grilling on the weekend, or maybe going fishing, or even just putting on a record. But lately... well, when I get in those low moods, I just sort of leave the stuff sitting there. I just don't really care to do any of it. 

It's not that I'm completely miserable or anything! I just... I don't know, the drive just isn't there. Does that make sense? I'm trying to give you the right examples, I just don't want it to sound like I'm completely falling apart when I'm really doing okay overall. Is that the kind of thing you meant?
During these low periods, do you find yourself feeling unusually tired or like you don’t have the energy to do things, even if they’re simple tasks?

Um, yeah, I do get a bit tired. I mean, I really don't want to complain, because I know everyone gets worn out after a long day at work, right? It's probably totally normal. But... well, I guess lately, by the time I get home from the office, even just the really simple things feel like a lot. 

Like, just walking to the end of the driveway to check the mail, or... or putting a few plates in the dishwasher. It just feels like way more effort than it really should be. I still get it done, mostly! I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around doing nothing. It just takes a bit more out of me than usual, I guess. Is that... is that helpful? I hope I'm not just whining about normal everyday stuff.
Do you find yourself feeling guilty or like you're not good enough almost every day, even when there's no specific reason for it?

Um, well... yeah, I guess I do feel that way a lot of the time. I mean, I think I mentioned this a little bit earlier, so I hope it's okay that I'm bringing it up again. I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right. 

But, yeah, it's like... almost every day, I just get this overwhelming feeling that I'm not really senior material at work. Even when nothing goes wrong, I just... I beat myself up over it. I start thinking that I've just tricked everyone into believing I can handle all these responsibilities, when really I can't. 

I know it's probably silly to feel guilty about something like that, especially when nobody has actually said anything bad about my work. I really try not to let it show, because I don't want to seem ungrateful for the position or anything. But... yeah, that guilt is just sort of always there in the background. Does that answer what you were asking? I can try to give a different example if that wasn't quite right.
During these low periods, do you find yourself moving more slowly than usual or feeling restless and unable to sit still?

Um... no, not really. I don't think I get restless or anything like that. I mean, I hope I'm not missing something important, but... I usually just try to stay focused on what I need to do, you know? 

And as for moving slowly... I guess I might take my time a bit more when I'm feeling tired, like I mentioned before, but I wouldn't say I'm moving in slow motion or anything dramatic like that. I still get around fine at the office and everything. I really try to keep a normal pace so I don't hold anyone else up. 

I'm sorry if that's not a very helpful answer. I just haven't really noticed either of those things happening. Is it... is it bad if I don't have that symptom? I can try to pay closer attention to it if you think I should be looking out for it.

Have you ever experienced sudden episodes where you feel intense fear or discomfort that comes on very quickly, like your heart racing, shortness of breath, or feeling like something terrible is going to happen?

Um, no, I don't think so. I haven't ever had anything quite like that happen. I mean, sure, if a server goes down at work or there's a big system issue, I might get a little stressed, but... but just normal stress, you know? Not like my heart is pounding out of my chest or I can't breathe or anything dramatic. I usually try to stay pretty calm under pressure so I don't worry the rest of the IT team. 

So, no, no sudden terror or anything like that. I hope it's okay that I keep saying no to some of these things. I'm really trying to give you the most accurate answers I can, I just... I don't want to make something up if it hasn't happened. Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you what you need for your notes.
During these low periods, do you find it harder to focus, make decisions, or think clearly, even when you're trying your best to stay on top of things?

Um... well, maybe just a little bit? But nothing too serious, I promise. I mean, when I'm feeling really down, it can take me a little longer to sort through a complex system architecture or figure out the best way to resolve an issue ticket. 

But I really try my hardest to push through it. I don't want to let my team down or make it seem like I'm slacking off. So I'll just double-check my work, or maybe read an email twice to make sure I got it right. I still get everything done, though. I haven't missed any deadlines or anything like that. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound incompetent. I really do try to stay on top of everything, even when it feels like my brain is a little foggy. Is it normal to have a little trouble focusing when you're feeling down? I just want to make sure I'm not making a big deal out of something everyone goes through.
During these low periods, do you ever feel like your thoughts are slowed down or that it’s harder to process things, even when you’re not tired?

Well... um, no, I don't think my thoughts actually slow down. Like, my brain still feels like it's running at its usual speed, you know? 

Even if I'm having a rough week, I can still process the system logs and figure out what's going wrong with the network just fine. I might be a little quieter than usual, but the gears are definitely still turning up there. I really pride myself on keeping my mind sharp so I don't mess up anything for the rest of the IT department. 

I hope that makes sense. I just... I want to be as helpful as possible, and I feel a little bad that I keep saying no to you. Is it alright that I don't have that happening? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information for your assessment.
During these low periods, do you find it harder to think clearly, concentrate, or make decisions, even when you're not distracted or tired?

Um... I think this might be a little bit like what you asked a minute ago, right? About the focus and everything? I really don't think I have much trouble with making decisions or concentrating, honestly. 

Like I mentioned, I might double-check my work just to be safe, but I can still map out a system upgrade or decide on the right security patches without any real problems. I don't just sit there unable to think or anything like that. 

I hope it's okay that my answer is basically the same as before. I just wouldn't say I lose my ability to concentrate, even when I'm feeling a bit low. I really hope I'm not being difficult by repeating myself! Am I doing okay with these questions? I just want to make absolutely sure I'm giving you what you need for your evaluation.
Do you ever feel like you’re a failure or that you’ve let people down, even when others don’t see it that way?

Um... well, maybe just a little bit? But I think that's just me trying to be realistic about my abilities, you know? 

I mean, I guess... well, actually, that's kind of why I came in to see you. I just... I keep beating myself up lately, thinking that I'm not really senior material. Like, I'll be sitting at my desk, and I just get this overwhelming feeling that I've somehow fooled everyone into thinking I can handle more than I actually can. 

But I try not to let it show! I still do my job, and I don't think my team has noticed anything. I just... I don't want to be a disappointment to them or to my boss. 

I hope that doesn't sound too pathetic. It's just hard sometimes, feeling like an imposter. Is it normal to feel that way when you're going through a rough patch? I really hope I'm not making a mountain out of a molehill here. I just want to be honest with you so you can do your assessment properly. Am I giving you the right kind of information?
Do you find that your confidence in yourself or your abilities is often lower than usual, even when there’s no clear reason for it?

Oh, um... yes. Actually, I think that's exactly what I was just trying to explain. I'm so sorry, I hope I didn't mess up the order of your questions by bringing it up a minute ago! 

But yeah, my confidence definitely drops. Like I was just saying, that's really the main reason I finally came in to see you. I just keep beating myself up, convincing myself that I'm not really senior material. I get this heavy feeling that I've just... fooled everyone into thinking I could handle more than I actually can. Even though, logically, nobody at work has actually complained about my systems analysis or anything. 

I'm sorry, I know I'm just repeating what I just told you. I hope that's alright? I just want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you're asking. Is that the kind of example you were looking for?
Do you find that you have little interest or pleasure in doing almost all of your usual activities, including things you used to enjoy?

Um... well, I wouldn't say I've lost interest in absolutely everything. I still try to keep up with things, you know? I really don't want to sound like I'm just sitting around doing nothing all day. 

But, I guess... if I'm being completely honest, I haven't really been doing the things I normally do to relax. Like, usually I really look forward to grilling on the weekend, or maybe going fishing, or even just putting on a good record in the evening to unwind. 

Lately, though, I just... I kind of just leave all that stuff sitting there. I'll look at the grill or my records and I just don't really care to bother with them right now. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound lazy! I'm sure it's just a temporary slump and I'll get back to my normal weekend routine soon. Is that... is that the kind of thing you're asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kinds of examples for your notes.
Do you find that your low mood is present most of the day, nearly every day, even when there’s nothing specific happening to cause it?

Um... well, I really try to keep a positive attitude, you know? I don't want to be someone who just sits around feeling sorry for myself, especially when there's no real reason for it. 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... yeah. Most days lately, I've just had this... this heavy, low feeling. It's hard to explain, but it's kind of like I'm just moving through work and home, but... like the color has been turned down on everything? 

I really hope that makes sense. I know I shouldn't complain when nothing is actually going wrong in my life, but it just sort of hangs around in the background almost all day. I'm trying my best to push through it, though! Is that... does that help with your assessment? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it the right way for you.
Do you find that you take little or no pleasure in most of the things you used to enjoy, even the ones that used to make you happy?

Oh, um... yes, I think we actually just touched on that a moment ago. I'm so sorry, I hope I'm not making your job harder by repeating myself! 

But yeah, like I mentioned with the grilling and the fishing... I usually really look forward to those things. And putting on a record after work, too. It's just that lately, I've been leaving all my gear and my records just sitting there. I just haven't really cared to do any of it. 

I really don't want you to think I'm just giving up on my hobbies or anything! I'm sure I'll get the spark back soon. I just... I hope it's okay that I brought up the same example again? Does that answer what you were asking?
Do you find that your low mood is present for most of the day, nearly every day, even when there’s nothing specific happening to cause it?

Oh, um... I think you might have just asked me that one, too. I'm so sorry, I hope I'm not confusing things or messing up your process! 

But yes, like I was saying before... I really try to stay positive, but most days lately I've just had this... this heavy, low feeling. It's like I'm just moving through work and home, but the color has been turned down on everything. 

I really don't want to sound like a complainer, especially since nothing is actually wrong in my life to cause it. I'm trying really hard to push past it. I hope it's okay that my answer is the same as before? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need for your notes.
